Researched on 26 November 2026 (India time).

## Company, role, location and posting

- **Role:** Founder’s Office: Revenue Operations & Systems (RevOps).
- **Location:** Bengaluru, onsite.
- **Posting URL:** [Employer’s Greenhouse posting and application form](https://job-boards.greenhouse.io/enterpret/jobs/8194486003).
- **Open status:** The employer’s [current openings board](https://job-boards.greenhouse.io/enterpret) lists this role, and the individual posting has an application form. Both opened successfully during this research.
- **Date posted:** **5 November 2026**, according to [GTM Daily](https://gtmdaily.com/jobs/founder-s-office-revenue-operations-systems-revops-enterpret-c3ab1a7a)—21 days before this research, within the requested 30-day window. The employer page does not display a posting date, so this is secondary-source evidence, not an employer-verified original publication date. GTM Daily’s outbound redirect failed to resolve in the browsing tool; the employer URL above was independently opened from its own job board.
- **Experience:** [Placement Baba](https://placementbaba.com/job/founder-s-office-revenue-operations-systems-revops-at-enterpret-in-bengaluru-141270) explicitly labels this opening **0–3 years**. **Responsibilities:** Diagnose revenue-process failures; improve lead assignment, deals, renewals and departmental transfers. Repair CRM problems, reconcile records and produce decision-useful metrics. Assist forecasts and planning. Align commercial records with Finance without independently committing policy or money. Develop, validate and monitor AI-enabled automation; coordinate delivery and document maintainable processes.

**Requirements:** Demonstrated operational ownership; practical CRM knowledge; spreadsheet and SQL analysis; API or low-code integration skills; evaluated AI use; judgment, learning ability, communication and dependable execution.

The experience band remains a secondary-source claim, so this should not be treated as an unqualified eligibility match.

Enterpret’s employer board names Kleiner Perkins and Sequoia as backers, supporting the preference for an established venture-backed startup. [Source: employer careers board](https://job-boards.greenhouse.io/enterpret).

# T0012 (attempt 2): both review points are fixed. Pull request: https://github.com/shloki-loki/CATE/pull/4 (commit 33b230c)

It's ready for you to merge, and merging deploys it. I can't merge to `main` myself.

## 1. Shift+Enter no longer numbers or bullets lists
- In the chat box, **Shift+Enter now always gives a plain new line**. This holds after `1. one`, `- item`, `- [ ] task` or `3) third`. Nothing is added to the next line.
- **Enter still sends.** Enter doesn't send while a character is still being composed in an input method (IME), such as Japanese.
- I removed the list feature completely: the code (`web/lib/listContinue.mjs`), its tests and the "Auto lists: on/off" switch under the chat box.
- Your browser may have saved "on" from the first version of this pull request. That setting is now ignored and deleted when the page loads, so it can't turn the feature back on.
- The key handling now lives in `web/lib/composerKeys.mjs`. Only the send keypress is blocked. Shift+Enter is left to the browser.
- New tests replace the ones that checked for numbering:
  - `web/tests/composerKeys.test.mjs` checks for a plain new line after numbered, bulleted and checkbox items and after empty items. It also checks that Enter sends and that the Enter that finishes an IME character neither sends nor is blocked.
  - `tests/test_web_ui.py` checks that the key handler blocks only the send keypress and that none of the old list code or saved setting is left.

## 2. The "Get a key ↗" link now works from the keyboard
- On the Models page, the provider cards (Groq, Gemini, …) under "Which API?" were the problem. The link sat inside a clickable card, and the card cancelled Enter.
- Now each card has a real button that picks the provider, and the "Get a key" link sits beside that button, not inside it. The card handler is gone.
- Enter on the focused link opens the key page in a new tab and leaves the selected provider unchanged.
- Space or Enter on a provider's button picks it. Tab moves from a provider to its link.
- The cards look the same as before; I checked a screenshot of the add section.

## Also
I merged the latest `main`, which brings in pull request #3. All other parts of the redesign are unchanged; the reviewer had passed them. They are the top-right brightness button, the removed archived-projects switch, the "Add a model or API" section, the home page, the team map and the colours.

## Testing
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`: **26 tests, OK**.
- `cd web && npm ci && npm run build`: **passed**. `npm test`: **6/6 passed**.
- I ran the site locally against a copy of the data and tested it in headless Chromium: **24/24 checks passed**.
  - **Chat box, in a fresh browser:** Shift+Enter after each of the 4 list lines gives exactly the line plus a new line. Typing "1. one", Shift+Enter, "two" gives `1. one` and `two` on the next line with no number. There's no list switch.
  - **Chat box, in a browser with "on" saved from before:** the same results, and the old setting gets deleted.
  - **Enter** sent a test message, which showed up as a new project.
  - **Models page:** Enter on the focused "Get a key" link wasn't blocked. It opened the provider's key page in a new tab (aistudio.google.com/apikey, which redirected to Google sign-in), and the selected provider stayed Groq. Picking a provider with Space or Enter worked, and so did Tab from a provider to its link.
  - **Other pages:** there's no "Show archived" control. The brightness button sits 12px from the right edge and 9.5px from the top, and clicking it switched light to dark.
- What I couldn't test: Safari, Firefox, a real phone, or the live Vercel site. The Chromium test script isn't committed because it needs a browser installed.

The opt-out requires users to change a setting. I confirmed the focused link's Enter event was canceled in Chromium. Separate the link from the radio control or restrict the handler to the card itself. Verify keyboard users can activate the link independently of provider selection.

**Verification.** The Python suite passed all 25 tests, npm test passed all six tests, and npm ci and the production build succeeded. The numbered and bulleted list tests explicitly assert continuation, so a green suite currently enforces the failed behavior.

result.text:
Implemented the independent audit in [pull request #3](https://github.com/shloki-loki/CATE/pull/3). Run `python3 -m cate.audit` from the checkout to generate the chat report. The command runs locally and uses fixed, sourced competitor profiles.

All 22 tests passed with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`. The new tests run the CLI, check the required Markdown sections and competitors, and exercise the scan against broken and valid source fixtures.

# CATE product audit

## Feature Checklist

Each check marks implementation evidence in this checkout.

- [x] Project chat and attachments — `web/app/actions.js:133`
- [x] Send the same prompt to multiple models — `web/app/actions.js:137`
- [x] Review a plan before starting its steps — `web/app/actions.js:203`
- [x] Add model connections — `web/app/actions.js:291`
- [x] Choose a model for a task — `cate/core.py:109`
- [x] Gate dispatch on account availability — `cate/core.py:61`
- [x] Check cross-provider review eligibility — `cate/core.py:179`
- [x] Track run usage and limits — `cate/core.py:249`
- [x] Recover stalled work — `cate/core.py:268`
- [x] Restore browser drafts per project — `web/components/Chat.js:21`

## Bug Summary

Inspected 9 Python and 25 dashboard source files. Checks cover unresolved Python names and module imports, literal internal routes, interval cleanup and retained module caches. Findings need runtime verification.

- `web/lib/store.js:41` Module cache `cache` retains entries. Check whether the key set and retained values stay bounded.
- `web/lib/store.js:126` Module cache `mainCache` retains entries. Check whether the key set and retained values stay bounded.

### Conversation continuity

The worker prompt selects one project by chat ID and includes up to 24 recent messages (`cate/cli.py`, `conversation`). Instructions in another project or earlier in a long conversation can drop out of this handoff. Try a saved, user-editable project brief and check whether a second worker can recall a preference from it.
The dashboard supervisor receives up to 30 messages from the active chat (`web/lib/supervisor.js`, `history`). Reopening a saved chat and carrying context into a new project are separate behaviors to test.

## Competitor Analysis

These fixed examples use named 2024 model releases so the vendor measurements have a clear baseline. The reusable-context examples come from separate product documentation.

### OpenAI ChatGPT · GPT-4o

GPT-4o processes speech, images and text in one neural network. A person can ask about a photo in chat, a shorter interaction than submitting an attachment and waiting for a CATE worker. OpenAI reported a 320 ms average response to audio input, a model-level figure. ChatGPT Projects also lets related chats reuse project files and instructions. [GPT-4o launch](https://openai.com/index/hello-gpt-4o/) · [ChatGPT Projects](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10169521-projects-in-chatgpt)

### Google Gemini Advanced · Gemini 1.5 Pro

Gemini uses a mixture of experts inside the model. CATE selects entire models for individual tasks. Gemini Advanced lets a user attach files from Drive or a device and ask about them together. Google reported 99% retrieval of a planted fact in its test with inputs up to one million tokens. That test measures recall within one input. For continuity across chats, a user can save instructions and reference files in a Gem. [Model and evaluation](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/products/google-gemini-next-generation-model-february-2024/) · [Gemini Advanced workflow](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gemini/google-gemini-update-may-2024/) · [Reusable Gems](https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/15146780?hl=en)

### Anthropic Claude · Claude 3.5 Sonnet

Claude pairs a hosted vision-and-text model with Artifacts, a pane for inspecting and revising generated work alongside the chat. A user can check the result while discussing it. Anthropic reported twice the speed of Claude 3 Opus and stronger results on its vision evaluations. CATE adds a different quality check by sending completed work to a separate reviewer. [Sonnet and Artifacts](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-3-5-sonnet)

### What to measure in CATE

Run the same document question and revision through direct chat and a reviewed CATE task. Record time to first answer, time to accepted result, charges or subscription tokens, and errors caught by review. A second chat with the same project instructions tests continuity. Use a non-secret preference for the recall test. These vendor measurements cover different tasks and cannot establish a CATE performance ranking.

# Review of T0013 (PR #3, gpt-1): PASS, score 88

## How I checked
- I read the whole diff with `gh pr diff 3`. It changes 3 files: `cate/audit.py` (new), `tests/test_audit.py` (new) and one README line.
- I checked out commit 5c8dd14 and ran `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` with Python 3.14. 22 tests ran and all passed.
- `python3 -m cate.audit` exited 0, printed 48 lines and wrote nothing to stderr.
- `web/` is not touched, so no npm build was needed.

## Checks
1. **Script runs without exceptions: PASS.** The CLI exits 0. Files that fail to parse or read are reported as findings and do not crash the run.
2. **Report has Feature Checklist, Bug Summary and Competitor Analysis sections: PASS.** These are the only three `##` headings, in that order.
3. **Competitor list has at least 3 major platforms: PASS.** It covers OpenAI ChatGPT/GPT-4o, Google Gemini 1.5 Pro and Anthropic Claude 3.5 Sonnet.
   - The text is hard-coded and covers architecture, UI/UX and performance for each.
   - Each one links to vendor sources.
   - The figures match the vendors' published claims as far as I know: GPT-4o's 320 ms average audio response, Gemini 1.5's MoE design and 99% retrieval up to 1M tokens, and Sonnet 3.5 at twice the speed of Claude 3 Opus. It also warns that these figures can't rank CATE's performance.
4. **Unit test validates the output format: PASS.**
   - `test_module_prints_chat_report` runs the CLI as a subprocess. It asserts the exact heading list, at least one checked item and the three platform subheadings.
   - A second test builds a fixture tree and checks each detector both ways (finds the problem, accepts valid code). It covers syntax errors, missing relative imports, unresolved names, dead routes (with dynamic routes, redirect aliases and public files allowed), interval cleanup and Map caches. It also confirms that `data/` is not scanned.

## Good
- The scan only reads source. It uses `ast`/`symtable` and never imports or runs the code it scans.
- Feature checklist rows are backed by markers found in the code, with real line numbers. I checked a sample, e.g. `cate/core.py:109 def choose_model(`. A row turns unchecked if the feature disappears.
- Bug findings are worded honestly as candidates that need runtime verification. I checked the two flagged caches in `web/lib/store.js`. They are real module-level Maps with no eviction, keyed by file name, so they are bounded in practice. Flagging them for a human to look at is fair.
- It keeps out of `./data`, which matters for privacy.

## Minor, not blocking
- The brief names "GPT-4-Vision"; the PR uses GPT-4o, its successor. Acceptable.
- The Claude architecture note ("hosted vision-and-text model") is thin next to the other two.
- `sys.stdlib_module_names` needs Python 3.10 or later. CI uses 3.12, so this is fine.
- The import check would flag third-party packages. CATE is stdlib-only today, so it's harmless.
- The "memory leak" checks are simple heuristics (setInterval, `new Map()` with `.set` and no delete). They are labelled that way.
